12.1.name: JAM.AccState
12.1.note: ξ is the field `accumulated`, one `OctetSet` per block of the epoch

12.3.name: JAM.AccState
12.3.note: ω is the field `ready`, one list of `JAM.ReadyEntry` per slot of the epoch

12.8.name: JAM.readyOrder
12.8.note: well-founded recursion on the queue length: each round shrinks it (`JAM.editQueue_length_lt`)

12.15.name: JAM.PartialState
12.15.note: the privileges χ are flattened into `manager`, `assigners`, `delegator`, `registrar` and `alwaysAcc`

12.16.name: JAM.accPar
12.16.at: (PartialState × List DeferredTransfer × List (Nat × List UInt8) × List (Nat × Nat))
12.16.note: B is `List (Nat × List UInt8)` and U is `List (Nat × Nat)`; B is a set in the paper, made one when θ′ is built in `JAM.accumulate`

12.17.name: JAM.partitionXfers
12.17.note: this is T*; `JAM.accSeq` calls it with `[]` for ∅, which is T

12.18.name: JAM.accSeq
12.18.note: gas is an `Int`; the rounds are bounded by fuel, and running out is the error `fuelExhausted`; no theorem yet shows the bound is never reached (note v0.8.1-A47)

12.19.name: JAM.accPar
12.19.note: N is `JAM.discardIfBoth`, R is `JAM.pick`, and a new-index conflict in **n** is an error (`JAM.collectNew`)

12.21.name: JAM.integrateProvisions
12.21.note: applies the provisions one at a time, testing Y against the accounts updated so far

12.25.name: JAM.accumulate
12.25.at: let (n, e', b, u, t) ← accSeq
12.25.note: g is the binding `let g : Nat :=` two lines above

12.27.name: JAM.accumulate
12.27.note: `e'` is the partial state returned by `JAM.accSeq`; its accounts δ‡ are replaced by `accounts`, δ‡ with eq. 12.30 applied

12.28.name: JAM.AccStat
12.28.note: the statistics are `AccResult.stats : List (Nat × AccStat)`, in ascending order of service

12.34.name: JAM.accumulate
12.34.note: entry `idx` is ω′↻₍m−i₎ with i = (m − idx) mod E

12.36.name: JAM.preimagesOrdered
12.36.note: strictly ascending in `JAM.preimageLt`: by service, then by the data octets
